title: Cross-Chain Client Gateway for CCIP-Read
description: An extension of CCIP-Read where the client itself performs a cross-chain read named by an x-chain URL
body:
## Abstract

This ERC extends [ERC-3668](./eip-3668.md) so a contract can ask the client to read another contract directly, on another chain or the same chain, instead of relying on an offchain gateway. The client returns the same result a gateway would, using its own trusted connection to that chain, so no third party is involved. Contracts can also detect clients that do not support this ERC.

## Motivation

An [ERC-3668](./eip-3668.md) gateway must either be trusted or return a proof that the contract verifies on the original chain. In many cases a valid proof cannot be produced. That does not make the read unsafe. A client that already trusts its RPC connection to the destination chain can make the call itself.

This ERC lets the client act as the gateway. The contract names the chain and contract to read, and the client answers using its own trusted RPC, so no third party is involved.

## Specification

The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119 and RFC 8174.

In this ERC, an Interoperable Address is a version 1 [ERC-7930](./eip-7930.md) Interoperable Address.

### The x-chain URL

An `x-chain` URL has the following form.

```
x-chain:0x<interoperable-address>[?finalized=<value>]
```

`<interoperable-address>` is the lowercase hexadecimal encoding of an Interoperable Address containing both a chain reference and a target address. The `AddressLength` field MUST NOT be zero. The hexadecimal string MUST be lowercase and MUST contain no bytes beyond the end of the Interoperable Address.

For example, the following URL names the contract `0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913` on Base, chain id 8453.

```
x-chain:0x0001000002210514833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913
```

A URL that is not well formed under this section is unsupported. A client that supports this ERC handles an unsupported `x-chain` URL as defined under Client behavior.

#### The finalized parameter

The OPTIONAL `finalized` query parameter selects the block at which the call is made. When it is present with a non-empty value, for example `?finalized=true` or `?finalized=1`, the client makes the call at the finalized block. Otherwise the client makes the call at the latest block. If the client cannot serve the finalized block on the destination chain, the call MUST fail, and the client MUST NOT fall back to the latest block.

The callback does not learn which block was used, because the response does not include block metadata. A contract that needs the block number MUST have the remote function return it.

### Contract behavior

A contract requests a cross-chain read by reverting with the `OffchainLookup` error defined in [ERC-3668](./eip-3668.md), with the `x-chain` URL in `urls` and with `callData` set to the plain call data for the target contract. No wrapping or envelope is applied to `callData`.

The contract SHOULD place a `data:` URL after the `x-chain` URL as a fallback for clients without support for this ERC. A client that supports this ERC never uses it.

```
data:application/json,{"data":"0xff"}
```

The callback MUST treat a one byte `0xff` response as a client without support for this ERC, never as a remote result. Successful responses MUST be decoded as `bytes` before interpreting the remote return data.

### Client behavior

A client that supports this ERC MUST use the first `x-chain` URL in `urls` and ignore all other URLs.

The client alone decides whether it can safely make the call on the destination chain. This includes knowing the chain, having a trusted RPC endpoint for it, and supporting its virtual machine. The client MUST use its own RPC endpoints and MUST NOT take endpoints or chain metadata from the contract. Support for one EVM chain does not imply support for another. If the client cannot make the call, or the URL is unsupported, it MUST fail the call, the same outcome as a gateway HTTP 4xx response.

The client calls the target contract on the destination chain with `callData`, at the selected block. The destination chain MAY be the same chain.

To keep a consistent view of destination-chain state, the client MUST select the block once per `x-chain` read and use that same block for all destination-chain read-only contract calls belonging to that read, including callbacks. For `latest`, the client MUST identify the block by hash or by an equivalent mechanism that guarantees every call uses that same block. On EVM chains, [EIP-1898](./eip-1898.md) provides block-hash selection for `eth_call`. If the client cannot guarantee this or cannot serve the selected block, it MUST fail the read.

- On success, the client MUST invoke the callback of the contract that requested the `x-chain` read with `abi.encode(result)`, where `result` is the final destination-chain return data, typed as `bytes`.
- On a revert, the client MUST fail the call and SHOULD surface the revert data.
- On an `OffchainLookup` revert from the target contract, the client handles it as a normal [ERC-3668](./eip-3668.md) lookup on the destination chain and MUST pass gateway responses unchanged to their callbacks. If that lookup or any subsequent destination-chain lookup includes an `x-chain` URL, including inside a batch request, the client MUST fail the enclosing `x-chain` read.

Lookups on the destination chain count toward the client's ERC-3668 lookup limit for the original call.

When processing an ENSIP-21 batch locally, the client MUST apply this ERC to each inner request. Remote batch gateways MUST NOT execute `x-chain` URLs and MUST continue with the next URL, if any, because executing them would replace the client's trusted RPC connection with the gateway's.

## Rationale

[ERC-3668](./eip-3668.md) does not require a gateway to be an HTTP service, and allows URLs of any scheme. The client already trusts its own RPC connections, so it can answer a cross-chain read without adding a third party. A client that supports this ERC ignores all other URLs, so it never sends the request to a third-party gateway. It returns the `eth_call` return data ABI-encoded as `bytes`. Nested `x-chain` URLs are not followed, which limits each call to one cross-chain hop and prevents loops between chains.

Clients that do not support this ERC can be detected with a `data:` URL rather than an HTTP gateway. Clients that skip unsupported URL schemes and support `data:` responses deliver `0xff` to the callback without any server or third party. A successful response is ABI-encoded `bytes` of at least 64 bytes, so it cannot equal the single byte `0xff`. The only block choice is latest or finalized, because other chains may not offer the same block tags, and finalized is the guarantee most contracts need. Contracts that must also serve clients without support for this ERC can operate their own gateway instead, at the cost of trusting that gateway, for example through a standard offchain signer.

## Backwards Compatibility

This ERC adds a URL scheme to the ERC-3668 `urls` list and changes no interfaces. Clients without support for this ERC return `0xff`, provided they support `data:` responses and continue to the next URL when a URL scheme is unsupported. Otherwise, the lookup may fail with an error.

## Test Cases

USDC on Base, chain id 8453, contract `0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913`.

```
x-chain:0x0001000002210514833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913
```

The ENS registry on Ethereum mainnet, chain id 1, contract `0x00000000000c2e074ec69a0dfb2997ba6c7d2e1e`, read at the finalized block.

```
x-chain:0x0001000001011400000000000c2e074ec69a0dfb2997ba6c7d2e1e?finalized=true
```

A contract that reads the USDC contract on Base reverts with `OffchainLookup` and this `urls` list.

```
[
  "x-chain:0x0001000002210514833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913",
  "data:application/json,{\"data\":\"0xff\"}"
]
```

- A client that supports this ERC uses the first URL. It calls the USDC contract on Base with `callData` and passes the ABI-wrapped result to the callback.
- A client that does not support this ERC skips the first URL and uses the second. It passes `0xff` to the callback.

## Reference Implementation

A contract that reads `totalSupply()` from USDC on Base.

```solidity
// SPDX-License-Identifier: CC0-1.0
pragma solidity ^0.8.24;

contract RemoteSupplyReader {
    error OffchainLookup(
        address sender,
        string[] urls,
        bytes callData,
        bytes4 callbackFunction,
        bytes extraData
    );
    error XChainUnsupported();

    string constant REMOTE_URL =
        "x-chain:0x0001000002210514833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913?finalized=true";
    string constant FALLBACK_URL = "data:application/json,{\"data\":\"0xff\"}";

    function remoteTotalSupply() external view returns (uint256) {
        string[] memory urls = new string[](2);
        urls[0] = REMOTE_URL;
        urls[1] = FALLBACK_URL;
        revert OffchainLookup(
            address(this),
            urls,
            abi.encodeWithSignature("totalSupply()"),
            this.remoteTotalSupplyCallback.selector,
            ""
        );
    }

    function remoteTotalSupplyCallback(
        bytes calldata response,
        bytes calldata
    ) external pure returns (uint256) {
        if (response.length == 1 && response[0] == 0xff) {
            revert XChainUnsupported();
        }
        bytes memory result = abi.decode(response, (bytes));
        return abi.decode(result, (uint256));
    }
}
```

## Security Considerations

The result is only as reliable as the client's RPC connection to the destination chain, and the contract cannot verify it, so contracts should not use it to authorize a state change without a proof. The same call can behave differently on different EVM chains, so a client that supports one chain should not assume it supports another. `latest` can be reorganized, especially on rollups, so contracts that act on the result should consider `?finalized=true`.
